title: 'There’s Gotta Be a Class for Old Men' — Marco Andretti Explains Why Young Talent Keeps Him From Returning to Grassroots Racing
excerpt:
Dale Earnhardt Jr. has found an unusual way to deal with missing NASCAR. Every few months, he gets into a Late Model, races against drivers at the local tracks and gets his fix. It is not a comeback, and he has no interest in racing every weekend again. He suggested Marco Andretti could do the same. But Andretti had one problem with that idea, and it had nothing to do with finding a car.

“There’s gotta be a class for old men”

“Like a go-kart class,” Andretti joked on The Dale Jr. Download. He had just explained why returning to grassroots racing was not so straightforward.

“The reason I would say no is because these kids are so damn good.”

That is where the conversation got interesting. Earnhardt was trying to convince Andretti that he did not need to return to prove anything. Andretti, however, could not separate getting back in a race car from the expectation of being competitive. “I just think you can’t half-ass that,” he said.

Earnhardt knows the feeling of wanting to race again. He admitted that retirement initially brought relief. Not having to wake up on Sunday and worry about performing was something he appreciated. But the longer he stayed away, the more he missed it.

Even now, a Late Model appearance can bring back the excitement, although halfway through a race, he sometimes remembers why he stopped.

His route out was different from Andretti’s. Earnhardt retired from full-time Cup competition after 2017 but continued making occasional starts in grassroots racing. Andretti, meanwhile, gradually stepped away from IndyCar.

After his final full-time season in 2020, he continued competing in the Indianapolis 500 and joined the Superstar Racing Experience (SRX), winning its 2022 championship. He announced his retirement in October 2025, having recorded two IndyCar victories in 253 starts and made 20 consecutive Indianapolis 500 appearances.

Yet Andretti has not stopped feeling the pull. He told Earnhardt that watching races brings back the adrenaline. There are moments when he desperately wants to be involved and others when he is glad to be on the couch. The difference is that he does not see an occasional start as something he can approach casually.

Earnhardt offered Chase Elliott as an example. The 2020 Cup champion went to the Chili Bowl Nationals, where he faced drivers who spend their careers racing indoor midgets. He got beaten, but that was never the point.

Elliott wanted to experience the event. Earnhardt recalled discussing it with Kevin Harvick, who credited Elliott’s willingness to take that chance with changing his own attitude toward grassroots racing.

For Earnhardt, that was the lesson. A former Cup driver should be able to enter a local race, get beaten and still enjoy the experience. But Andretti sees a different challenge. The competition is not waiting for established names to return. Young drivers are already pushing the standard, even in go-karts.

That is why the idea of a separate class for older racers sounded so appealing. Earnhardt has learned to enjoy racing without carrying the same expectations. Andretti has not quite reached that point.

He misses being behind the wheel, but facing a generation that keeps getting better makes returning on his own terms harder than he imagined.

This article first appeared on EssentiallySports and was syndicated with permission.

title: 1 day ago •Featured Inside Line Extra: Biggest 2027 Story at Arrow McLaren? Felix Rosenqvist (photo, left) and Scott Dixon (photo, right) are headed to Arrow McLaren in 2027 with a clear mission: win another Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge.
excerpt:
1 day ago

Note: This series gathers the Inside Line panel to discuss the major storyline surrounding each NTT INDYCAR SERIES team entering the 2027 season. An installment on each team will appear at INDYCAR.com on Fridays.

Curt Cavin: This one is straightforward: Arrow McLaren’s overhaul of its driver lineup is specifically designed to win the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge. Why else would Zak Brown and Tony Kanaan stock the cupboard with three former Indy winners to drive alongside this generation’s best driver never to win Indy (Pato O’Ward)? The signing of Scott Dixon (2008) and Felix Rosenqvist (2026) as the team brings back Ryan Hunter-Reay (2014) offers a terrific four-driver opportunity to win the sport’s biggest prize. In fact, I can make the argument Arrow McLaren, along with Team Penske, should be favored to put the next driver in Victory Lane. I know Brown well, and this is personal. He has masterfully overhauled McLaren in Formula One by winning a pair of Constructors’ titles and helping Lando Norris become a world champion, but he hasn’t completely cracked the INDYCAR code, especially at Indy. Brown, a Californian who was once on his own path to compete at Indy, is driven by that, and if the team can win Indy for the first time since 1976, well, that would complete the mission.

Eric Smith: Pato O’Ward is all-in on winning the Indianapolis 500 and an NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship. Meanwhile, Scott Dixon and Felix Rosenqvist’s moves to the team are worth watching, but will those signings ultimately propel O’Ward (photo, above) forward? That’s the thinking behind the changes. Christian Lundgaard finished third in the championship standings, ahead of O’Ward in fourth, but that wasn’t enough to save his job. The focus now shifts to O’Ward. He finished fourth in the 2026 championship, recording three victories, 10 top-five finishes and 11 top-10 results. He closed the season particularly strong, sweeping both races at Milwaukee Mile and earning three top-five finishes in the final five events. O’Ward has finished in the championship's top five in six of his seven full-time seasons. He recorded a career-best second-place finish in the standings in 2025 and has been the Indianapolis 500 runner-up twice. Which brings it all back to the free agent signings, and can they deliver O’Ward a championship and/or Indy 500 win in 2027?

Arni Sribhen: Arrow McLaren’s most consequential move of the 2027 Silly Season occurred behind the scenes rather than in the driver lineup, marked by the recruitment of Chris Simmons (photo, above, right) and Ross Bunnell from Chip Ganassi Racing’s engineering room. This high-profile acquisition anchors a multiyear technical department overhaul spearheaded by Zak Brown and Tony Kanaan. How this incoming pedigree integrates with the team's existing leadership – including Engineering Director Eric Cowdin, Technical Director Nick Snyder, and Will Anderson – will shape the upcoming season.

Paul Kelly: So many interesting storylines surrounding this team, but the most intriguing for me can’t be answered until next September at Laguna Seca: Did Arrow McLaren make a mistake releasing Christian Lundgaard? The Dane (photo, above, center) was third in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES standings and the highest-scoring driver on the team last season, edging mainstay Pato O’Ward by 13 points. Lundgaard’s haul of 535 points far outweighed the 412 and 331 points earned by 2027 signings Felix Rosenqvist and Scott Dixon at Meyer Shank Racing and Chip Ganassi Racing, respectively. Lundgaard has moved to Chip Ganassi Racing, the home of dominant four-time reigning champion Alex Palou. He will be insanely motivated to prove wrong McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown and Team Principal Tony Kanaan, who are putting all their proverbial eggs into one basket to win the Indy 500 with O’Ward and previous winners Dixon, Rosenqvist and Ryan Hunter-Reay. Arrow McLaren better succeed in that “500” quest, as I have a sneaking suspicion Lundgaard still may have the upper hand on the full-time Arrow McLaren trio in the standings when the 2027 season ends.

title: 2 DAYS AGO •Featured Let’s Cook Up Some Tasty Rivalries for 2027 Season
excerpt:
Rivalries are the lifeblood of sports. They create drama, fuel competition and give fans another reason to circle certain matchups on the calendar.

In motorsports, where competitors battle wheel-to-wheel at speeds exceeding 200 mph, those rivalries can become even more compelling. The NTT INDYCAR SERIES has experienced its share of heated exchanges, controversial moments and on-track confrontations throughout its history. But not every rivalry has to be fueled by animosity. Some are built on years of competition, contrasting personalities or simply two drivers who refuse to give an inch.

With a new season approaching, several intriguing storylines have the potential to develop into compelling rivalries in 2027. Here are five potential rivalries to watch.

Zak Brown vs. Chip Ganassi

If there's one rivalry on this list that already has some history behind it, this is it.

It's no secret that McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown (photo, above) and Chip Ganassi have their differences. Their relationship took a particularly contentious turn following the 2021 season, when McLaren attempted to lure Alex Palou from Chip Ganassi Racing after the Spaniard captured his first NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship.

What followed was a highly publicized contract dispute and legal battle that ultimately ended with Palou remaining at Ganassi. Since then, Palou has established himself as the dominant driver of the series, winning five championships in six seasons. But the competition between these two organizations hasn't been limited to the driver market.

Arrow McLaren has continued to strengthen its operation by bringing in personnel with deep ties to Ganassi, most notably six-time series champion Scott Dixon, who spent 25 years driving for CGR and earned 58 of his 59 career victories with the organization. In return, Ganassi signed Christian Lundgaard, the top points finishing Arrow McLaren driver in 2026, to replace Dixon.

There has also been speculation about additional Ganassi personnel potentially making the move to Arrow McLaren ahead of 2027. Whether those moves materialize or not, the underlying tension between team owners Brown and Ganassi provides plenty of intrigue. Both are accustomed to competing at the front, and neither is particularly interested in losing an advantage to the other.

Alex Palou vs. Christian Lundgaard

Sometimes, the most intriguing rivalry can develop between two drivers who share the same garage.

Lundgaard's move to Chip Ganassi Racing creates an especially interesting dynamic entering 2027. After two seasons with Arrow McLaren, the Dane was released despite delivering consistent results, including top-five championship finishes in each campaign.

His 2026 season was particularly impressive. Lundgaard won twice and finished third in the championship standings as McLaren's highest-placed driver. Yet, despite those accomplishments, he found himself looking for a new opportunity. He didn't have to look far to find one. Lundgaard joined Chip Ganassi Racing, where he will compete alongside Palou and Kyffin Simpson.

Palou has established himself as the driver to beat, and anyone joining Ganassi knows the expectations that come with sharing an organization with him. The opportunity for Lundgaard presents more than just a chance to compete for victories and championships. It's also an opportunity to measure himself against one of the best drivers in the world.

Lundgaard has previously been vocal about his ambitions to catch Palou, making their new teammate relationship even more compelling. He arrives with something to prove after his departure from McLaren, and he has the talent and experience to make things interesting.

David Malukas vs. Andretti Global

Not every rivalry needs bad blood. Sometimes, a little friendly competition dating back to childhood is more than enough.

Kyle Kirkwood and David Malukas have competed against each other for much of their racing careers. Their rivalry dates to 2009, when both began racing karts in Florida. They continued crossing paths throughout the junior formula ranks before emerging as the two dominant drivers of the 2021 INDY NXT by Firestone season.

That year, Kirkwood and Malukas (photo, above) combined to win 17 of the 20 races on the schedule, with Kirkwood ultimately claiming the championship by 13 points. Both drivers then made their way to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES as members of the 2022 rookie class.

Now, their careers have taken them to two of the series' most prominent organizations. Kirkwood competes for Andretti Global, while Malukas joined Team Penske in 2026.

Both drivers have the talent and equipment to contend for race victories and championships, making the possibility of a season-long battle between the longtime competitors especially intriguing. They know each other's strengths, have shared plenty of competition throughout their development and understand what it takes to beat one another. There's plenty of respect between the two, but don't expect either to give the other an inch when a victory is on the line.

Speaking of respect, Malukas faces another potential rivalry as he looks to fill some enormous shoes at Team Penske. Malukas took over the No. 12 Chevrolet following Will Power's departure from the organization after a 17-year partnership that produced two series championships (2014, 2022) and a 2018 Indianapolis 500 victory.

Power also earned 65 of his series-record 71 NTT P1 Awards with Team Penske, along with 42 of his 45 career race victories. He joined Andretti Global for the 2026 season and beyond. Replacing a driver with that kind of resume and history is no small task.

But Malukas already has given the comparison an interesting twist. In 2026, he finished fifth in the championship standings, ahead of Power, who placed 11th. Malukas also emerged as Team Penske's highest-finishing driver in the standings.

Power hasn't been shy about having a little fun with the comparisons, either. Now entering his second season with Andretti Global, the veteran has occasionally joked about Malukas taking over his former seat. With the two competing for separate powerhouse organizations, there's certainly potential for some added motivation whenever they share the track.

Christian Rasmussen vs. The Field

Christian Rasmussen has never been one to shy away from a fight on the racetrack. That approach has earned him plenty of attention from his competitors, not all of it positive.

The Danish driver (photo, above, left) has developed a reputation for aggressive racing, particularly on ovals, where his willingness to make bold moves has made him one of the more entertaining competitors in the field. Not everyone has appreciated that approach.

Rasmussen has drawn criticism from fellow drivers over some of his on-track decisions, but he hasn't shown much interest in changing his style. From his perspective, aggression is part of what makes him competitive, and backing down isn't necessarily part of the equation.

His oval performances have offered plenty of evidence to support that confidence. Rasmussen captured his first NTT INDYCAR SERIES victory at the Milwaukee Mile in 2025, showcasing the pace and racecraft that have made him a driver to watch on shorter ovals.

As he enters his third full-time season with ECR, Rasmussen will look to build on that success while continuing to establish himself as one of the series' rising talents.

Marcus Armstrong vs. Felix Rosenqvist

Armstrong wasn’t particularly thrilled with having to battle wheel-to-wheel against his 2026 Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian teammate Felix Rosenqvist for the win in last year’s Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge.

Armstrong led the field to the Lap 199 restart, but Malukas powered past both drivers on the final lap, while Rosenqvist went to the outside of Armstrong to battle for second during the 2.5-mile trip around the track. The two ran side-by-side for more than 20 seconds, but Armstrong (photo, above, left) eventually had to lift to preserve both cars and give at least one of them a chance to win. Rosenqvist (photo, above, right) capitalized.

There was no bad blood between the teammates, but Armstrong was understandably disappointed to see his opportunity for both his first INDYCAR SERIES victory and an Indianapolis 500 triumph slip away.

Rosenqvist moves to Arrow McLaren, while Armstrong remains with MSR but takes over the No. 60 entry. Mick Schumacher, meanwhile, moves from Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing to replace Armstrong in the No. 66 Honda.

With the seat change comes an inevitable set of comparisons to Rosenqvist. The Swede took the No. 60 from 25th in the standings to 12th in his first season with the team in 2024. He followed that with a sixth-place finish in 2025 before slipping to ninth last season, albeit with a victory in the year's biggest race.

title: Penske extends two-time champion Josef Newgarden
excerpt:
Team Penske announced a multi-year extension with two-time NTT IndyCar Series champion Josef Newgarden on Wednesday.

Terms were not disclosed but Penske said the deal will keep the two-time Indianapolis 500 winner in the No. 2 Chevrolet "for years to come."

"Josef Newgarden is one of the best drivers of his generation and has delivered in every aspect for our team for over a decade," said Jonathan Diuguid, president of Team Penske, IndyCar. "He is a two-time Indianapolis 500 winner and two-time IndyCar Series champion who wins for Team Penske and our partners on and off the track. We are thrilled to announce his extension and look forward to continuing that winning tradition for many years. With this extension, Team Penske has the strongest driver lineup in the paddock with Josef, Scott McLaughlin and David Malukas that will position us well for the future."

Newgarden, 35, has earned 31 wins since joining Penske in 2017, including series titles in 2017 and 2019 and back-to-back victories in the Indy 500 in 2023 and 2024.

"I've had the great privilege of driving for Team Penske for over a decade now," Newgarden said. "This is an exciting time for the IndyCar Series as we build towards a robust future for our sport with our partners and fans. My greatest enjoyment has been working with the men and women on this team, our partners, and pushing each other forward each day in an effort to produce results. It's been an honor to work with my fellow team members, and I'm excited to see what we can produce together in this next chapter."

Newgarden extended his streak to 12 straight seasons with at least one victory in 2026 by taking the checkered flags at Phoenix on March 7 and Illinois on June 7. He finished eighth in the season standings.

The 2027 NTT IndyCar Series opens on the streets of St. Petersburg, Fla., on March 7.

title: ‘It’s for the privileged’: Alex Palou reveals the exact moment his ‘goal’ was ‘no longer F1’
excerpt:
Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images

Originally posted on HITC | By Ashley Hambly | Last updated Nov 18, 2026 5:38 AM ET

Alex Palou is one of the most gifted drivers in the world when it comes to racing single-seaters, and was keen on being an F1 driver from a very early age.

The five-time champion has turned into a force to be reckoned with on the IndyCar grid, with the Spaniard now setting his sights on a fifth consecutive title in the category next year following his 2026 championship rout.

Hailing from Barcelona, Formula 1 was naturally Palou’s end goal from a very early age. Fernando Alonso had just become a global sensation through his ability to end Michael Schumacher’s dominance of the sport, which inspired the next generation of Spanish drivers.

Of course, fate had other plans for Palou, and he recently revealed the moment he knew that specifically being an F1 driver was ‘no longer’ his goal in life.

Alex Palou just wanted to be a racing driver after realising F1 ‘wasn’t feasible’

Following the clinching of his fourth world title at the end of the 2025 IndyCar campaign, Palou joined illustrious company as one of only six drivers in history to secure a quadruple at the premier level of American open-wheel car racing.

His fifth this year would see the Spaniard move into third all-time, with only Scott Dixon (six titles) and A.J. Foyt (seven titles) ahead of him.

Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images

During a candid interview with Diari ARA in December last year, he was asked about his F1 aspirations, to which he outlined how it was always a goal during his karting days until his loyalties shifted as he got older.

“It was the only thing I had in mind when I was between 5 and 10 years old and karting,” he began. “It was what I saw on TV and what I wanted, but as I got older, around 13 or 14, I started to understand how this world worked.

“That there are only 20 seats in F1 and that it’s for the privileged: it doesn’t just depend on you, you also need who knows how many millions behind you.

“I understood that it wasn’t feasible, so my goal was no longer F1; it was to be a driver. I don’t care if it’s cars, trucks, tractors, or Formula 1 cars.”

Then asked how he got into IndyCar, the 25-time race winner replied: “I tried Formula 3, but it didn’t go well. Although it wasn’t a big deal for me, I was always thinking, ‘What else is there?’

“I went to Japan, and there the possibility of making the jump to IndyCar opened up. It was feasible. It depended on speed and results, not on the millions I had behind me.

“It was the biggest championship I could reach. After Formula 1, it has the most races, the most prestige, and is perhaps the hardest to win.”

Since reaching and dominating IndyCar, opportunities in F1 presented themselves in the form of the McLaren F1 team. Palou took part in several tests for the team in hopes of landing a seat, until a contract dispute unfolded between himself and the British racing team.

A future move to F1 remains uncertain and even unlikely following the saga with McLaren, with the dispute culminating in Palou, McLaren, and Chip Ganassi Racing reaching a confidential final settlement.

This article first appeared on HITC and was syndicated with permission.

title: OpenAI To Serve as Alex Palou’s Primary Sponsor in 2027
excerpt:
OpenAI and Chip Ganassi Racing have extended their partnership through the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season, with OpenAI serving as the full-season primary partner of the No. 10 Honda (photo, top) driven by five-time and defending NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Alex Palou.

The expanded agreement builds on a partnership that began in 2025 and has included strategic research collaboration, primary car sponsorship, technical development and a documentary short series produced by Box-to-Box Films. Palou and CGR have won two championships and 15 races since the partnership began, including the 2025 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge.

“It's incredible to have OpenAI back on our car and with our team, but now for a full season as my primary sponsor,” Palou said. “Super exciting, especially following an incredible 2026 season. Winning Long Beach together was a huge moment for us, personally, as well. I can't wait to see what we can do in this final year with the current chassis.”

OpenAI's expanded presence will continue a technical collaboration between the organizations, with both sides exploring opportunities to apply artificial intelligence and innovation on and off the racetrack.

“Extraordinary things happen when great people come together,” team owner Chip Ganassi said. “I don't look at this as your normal type of sponsorship. OpenAI is a frontier, and we all want to be part of it. I feel like we're hopping on a train going 200 miles an hour, and we're enjoying every bit of it. There's a lot of opportunity for us.”

Palou (photo, above) has won 25 races and earned 50 podium finishes since joining Chip Ganassi Racing in 2021. He is one of only three drivers in INDYCAR SERIES history to win at least five championships. Palou will be joined by Christian Lundgaard, driver of the No. 9 PNC Bank Honda, and Kyffin Simpson, driver of the No. 8 Sunoco Honda, as Chip Ganassi Racing pursues its seventh Indianapolis 500 victory and 19th series championship.

“We’re seeing an incredible acceleration in what AI can do and how it’s being applied, and our continued partnership with Chip Ganassi is a really exciting way to bring that to life,” said Colin Fleming, OpenAI chief marketing officer, business. “Outside of your traditional AI use cases, this is a wonderful opportunity to take our research and apply it in nontraditional ways, showcasing the breadth of what’s possible as AI continues to advance.”

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season begins Sunday, March 7 with the Grand Prix of St. Petersburg in Florida, live on FOX.

title: 3 DAYS AGO •Featured Inside Line: ECR Moment or Driver To Put in Spotlight?
excerpt:
Today’s question: ECR recently announced ambitious plans to add new simulation tools to its headquarters, one of the biggest upgrades since the team was founded in 2011. Which one of ECR's drivers or seasons do you think deserves an extra spotlight?

Curt Cavin: I like to think back to the days when Ed Carpenter was only a driver, and there are a lot of today’s fans who didn’t get to see how good he was on the ovals. He won his first race as a team owner at the end of the 2012 season – at Auto Club Speedway – but he had won a race the year prior at Kentucky Speedway in a car entered by Sarah Fisher Racing. I wonder if you’ve heard of the two drivers chasing him to the finish line. Their names: Dario Franchitti and Scott Dixon, both in Chip Ganassi Racing cars -- the same guys who followed him at the finish in 2012 at Auto Club (photo, above). The race at Kentucky was such a great win for Fisher’s small group, and it’s one of my favorite results of the post-unification era. Ed’s other win came in 2014 at Texas Motor Speedway, and the drivers immediately trailing him were Will Power, Juan Pablo Montoya, Simon Pagenaud, Dixon and Tony Kanaan, with Helio Castroneves looming close. Think Ed couldn’t wheel it?! I’d also put his Indy 500 speed against almost anyone. He has won three poles, started on the front row five times and finished second to Power in 2018.

Eric Smith: It’s 2014, the first season that Ed Carpenter stepped out of the car on a full-time basis within his own team. Carpenter handled the oval races, while Mike Conway (photo, top) took over for the road and street courses. The arrangement paid off, with the No. 20 Chevrolet earning three victories -- two by Conway and one by Carpenter. Conway secured the team’s first road course victory at Long Beach, the second race of the season, before adding another win later that year at Toronto. Carpenter claimed his victory in the eighth race of the season at Texas. That set the tone for what ECR has become over a decade later.

Arni Sribhen: In 2016, Ed Carpenter Racing evolved from an underdog capable of snagging occasional wins into a legitimate contender against the INDYCAR SERIES’ established powerhouses. Leading the charge was Josef Newgarden (photo, above), who finished fourth in the standings as the highest-placing driver outside of Team Penske. His season was defined by grit, highlighted by a dominant victory at Iowa just weeks after breaking his collarbone and hand in a terrifying crash at Texas Motor Speedway. Newgarden’s teammates also delivered standout performances. Reigning INDY NXT champion Spencer Pigot stepped in as a rookie on the road courses and notched a pair of top-10 finishes, while JR Hildebrand enjoyed a strong Month of May – finishing sixth in the Indy 500 to secure two top-six results for the team.

Paul Kelly: My colleagues all walked longer down Memory Lane than me with this question. I’m choosing the team’s most recent moment of glory – Christian Rasmussen’s dramatic first career victory in 2025 at the Milwaukee Mile. Let’s face it: ECR was nowhere entering that weekend, with Rasmussen 13th and teammate Alexander Rossi 16th in points. Rasmussen showed promise by finishing third earlier in the season at World Wide Technology Raceway, while Rossi’s best result was fifth at Portland. But then Rasmussen drove from 10th on the starting grid to victory by taking fresh Firestone Firehawk tires during a rain delay and tracking down reigning series champion and pole sitter Alex Palou, passing him with 16 laps to go and running away to victory. Rossi finished a season-best fourth in the best result for ECR in ages and my favorite race result of 2025 amid the Palou-Ganassi steam roller.

title: 4 DAYS AGO •Driver News Josef Newgarden Signs Multiyear Contract Extension With Team Penske
excerpt:
Josef Newgarden will continue driving for Team Penske, as the two-time Indianapolis 500 winner and two-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion has signed a multiyear contract extension with the organization.

The agreement, announced Nov. 18, will keep the 35-year-old Tennessean behind the wheel of the No. 2 Chevrolet, extending a partnership that began in 2017 and has produced 31 INDYCAR SERIES victories – second most in Team Penske history behind Will Power’s 42 – and two championships. Newgarden made an immediate impact in his first season with Team Penske, winning the 2017 championship. He added a second series title in 2019 and reached the pinnacle of the sport with consecutive Indianapolis 500 victories in 2023 and 2024.

“Josef Newgarden is one of the best drivers of his generation and has delivered in every aspect for our team for over a decade,” said Jonathan Diuguid, president of Team Penske, INDYCAR and strategist for the No. 2 Chevrolet. “He is a two-time Indianapolis 500 winner and two-time INDYCAR SERIES champion who wins for Team Penske and our partners on and off the track. We are thrilled to announce his extension and look forward to continuing that winning tradition for many years.

“With this extension, Team Penske has the strongest driver lineup in the paddock with Josef, Scott McLaughlin and David Malukas, which will position us well for the future.”

Newgarden (photo, above) continued his remarkable run of winning seasons in 2026, extending his streak to 12 consecutive years with at least one victory. He won twice this past season, at Phoenix Raceway and World Wide Technology Raceway, finishing eighth in the championship standings. His two victories brought his career total to 34, tying him for ninth on the all-time INDYCAR SERIES wins list and making him the winningest active American driver in the series.

“I’ve had the great privilege of driving for Team Penske for over a decade now,” Newgarden said. “This is an exciting time for the INDYCAR SERIES as we build toward a robust future for our sport with our partners and fans. My greatest enjoyment has been working with the men and women on this team, our partners, and pushing each other forward each day in an effort to produce results. It’s been an honor to work with my fellow team members, and I’m excited to see what we can produce together in this next chapter.”

Newgarden also strengthened his standing as one of the most accomplished oval drivers in series history in 2026. He has 18 career oval victories, with wins at every oval on the current schedule except the Milwaukee Mile, which returned to the series in 2024. Newgarden and the No. 2 Chevrolet team begin their pursuit of a third INDYCAR SERIES championship when the 2027 season opens Sunday, March 7, on the streets of St. Petersburg.

title: ‘I don’t get what’s up with Tennessee’ – The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman drops comment that will catch the attention of Vols fans
excerpt:
No one seems to understand why the Tennessee Vols have been ranked below the Alabama Crimson Tide in the College Football Playoff rankings.

You can add The Athletic’s Bruce Feldman to the list of people who are “perplexed” by the way the College Football Playoff committee is handling Tennessee.

The Vols were ranked five spots below Alabama in last week’s College Football Playoff rankings despite having the same record as the Crimson Tide.

Oh, and Tennessee beat Alabama by 16 points a month ago.

“Thing that kind of has me perplexed is I don’t get what’s up with Tennessee and why they have disrespected them,” said Feldman on The Next Round. “I think Alabama’s good. I think just based off of what Tennessee has done, though, they shouldn’t be that far apart. And I hate when they do this thing that I noticed they started doing last year, relative to Miami and Notre Dame. It’s like, Oh, we can’t like look at them the same way or evaluate them against each other just because they’re too far apart in pods.’

“They treat Tennessee like Tennessee’s in the Sun Belt or in the MAC with the same record and the head-to-head win. It just doesn’t make sense to me in that regard.”

Tennessee has a 76% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 5% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 15, 2026).

The national media isn’t usually quick to come to Tennessee’s defense — which is how you know that the committee has been getting it all wrong with the Vols the last couple of weeks.

It’s going to be interesting to see what the committee does on Tuesday night when the new rankings are revealed. There are some folks who think it’s possible they’ll drop Tennessee a spot despite the Vols’ 22-7 win over Texas A&M in College Station.

title: No Smiths in ‘500,’ But This Smith’s Role Etched in Race’s Rich History
excerpt:
There have been 808 drivers who have made at least one start in the Indianapolis 500. Not one has had the surname Smith.

Meet Reid Smith, a Charlotte, North Carolina-based engraver whose work has become a permanent part of Indy 500 history. While Smith has never competed in the race, his hands have helped preserve its legacy, one engraving at a time.

Since 2021, Smith has been responsible for engraving the name, winning year and race-winning average speed of Indianapolis 500 winners on the base of the iconic Borg-Warner Trophy, the hardware every driver dreams of seeing adorned with their likeness.

“Just kind of ironic that your most common surname, certainly in America and parts of Europe, has never appeared among the race’s winners,” Smith said.

On Nov. 16, Smith added more words to the trophy, engraving Felix Rosenqvist’s name, winning year and race-winning average speed (photo, above) following one of the most dramatic finishes in the event’s history. Rosenqvist earned his place on the trophy by winning the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge on May 24. He made a daring move on the final lap in the No. 60 Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian Honda, using the high line against the wall exiting Turn 4 to power past David Malukas just yards before the Yard of Bricks start-finish line. Rosenqvist won by .0233 of a second, the closest finish in Indianapolis 500 history.

This latest assignment for Smith offered another opportunity to make a small but permanent contribution to the race’s history. It also brought an amusing connection to his own last name, which has roots in the very type of craftsmanship that defines his work.

“If you think about it, the surname Smith came from craftsman, like a blacksmith,” he said. “Rosenqvist’s do really cool things fast, and Smiths do very cool things slowly, and in metal.”

Blacksmiths worked with iron. Silversmiths worked with silver. And Smith, fittingly, works with the metal that helps tell the Indianapolis 500 story. He said the engraving itself is a tradition that requires a steady hand, an artistic eye and plenty of patience, leaving his approach anything but conventional.

Smith moves around the trophy rather than working methodically from top to bottom or left to right, sometimes starting with the bottom line before working his way through the rest of the design.

“Engraving is not like handwriting,” Smith said. “You’re not writing. It’s a design. It’s simply lines and curves. That’s all it is.”

Smith begins the process by designing the entire layout, marking the surface with wax and pencil. Starting at the top could mean accidentally rubbing away the design below as his hand moves across the trophy.

“The first thing that comes to mind is most of my projects are very small, and the Borg-Warner Trophy is very large, and it cannot be disassembled other than taking the bottom off of it,” Smith said. “That's actually the hardest part of the job, maneuvering the trophy while I'm working on it.”

Smith took over the responsibility in 2021, with Helio Castroneves' fourth "500" victory as his first engraving on the Borg-Warner Trophy.

On Nov. 17, the latest chapter in the trophy's annual transformation continued as the sterling silver face bearing Rosenqvist’s likeness was attached to the base by sculptor William Behrends. That process began months earlier.

On Sept. 22, Rosenqvist traveled to Tryon, North Carolina, where Behrends unveiled the sculpted clay likeness that will serve as the bas-relief portrait on the Borg-Warner Trophy. The iconic trophy features the likeness of every Indianapolis 500 winner, creating a visual history of the race dating to its inaugural running in 1911.

While Behrends captures the driver's likeness, Smith ensures the details of the victory are recorded for generations to come. Both crafts require precision, patience and an appreciation for the significance of the finished product.

“It continues to be amazing to me,” Smith said. “I enjoy being a part of it. All the people that I've worked with are so pleasant to deal with, and just knowing and learning more about the history, and just knowing that I'm a part of it is amazing. I remember it came to me afterward that: ‘Wow, that's going to be there forever, and no one can say I didn't do it. Or they can, but they'd be wrong.’

“Even though I was not a sports fan before working on this, I have continued to enjoy the excitement, not just because I'm a part of it, but I've found an enjoyment in the sport.”

title: Notes: New Andretti Sponsor To Back Power in 13 Races in 2027
excerpt:
Andretti Global announced Nov. 16 that zone Premium Nicotine Pouches, the latest innovation from ITG Brands, will serve as the primary partner of the No. 26 Honda entry driven by Will Power for 13 races of the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season.

The multiyear partnership marks zone’s INDYCAR debut, bringing together two brands focused on performance and innovation. Throughout the season, zone and Andretti Global will collaborate on marketing initiatives, content and fan engagement opportunities designed to connect the brand with adult nicotine consumers and the broader motorsports audience.

“I’m really excited to have zone on board in 2027,” Power said. “They’re a great fit for our team, and I think we’re going to have a lot of fun working together throughout the season. We showed a lot of speed last year, and the focus is on turning that into strong results starting in St. Pete.

“I can’t wait to see the new livery on track and get the No. 26 zone Premium Nicotine Pouches Honda to Victory Lane.”

Entering his second season with Andretti Global, Power (photo, top) brings more than two decades of INDYCAR SERIES experience and over 300 career starts to the partnership. The Australian is the series’ all-time leader in pole positions with 71 and ranks fourth in career victories with 45. A two-time INDYCAR SERIES champion (2014, 2022), Power has led more than 5,400 laps throughout his career and won the 102nd Running of the Indianapolis 500 in 2018.

zone branding on the No. 26 zone Premium Nicotine Pouches Honda will take to the track for the first time at the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season opener on the Streets of St. Petersburg, March 5-7, airing live on FOX.

“We are incredibly proud of what we’ve built with zone and excited about what’s ahead for the brand,” said Paola Pocci, ITG Brands president and CEO. :Partnering with Andretti Global and having a champion like Will Power behind the wheel is a significant step for zone, bringing together a brand defined by boldness and innovation with one of the most respected names in motorsports. This partnership reflects our continued commitment to investing in zone and taking the brand to new heights.”

WWTR Tickets On Sale

Tickets for the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES race at World Wide Technology Raceway are on sale at wwtraceway.com or by calling the ticket office at (618) 215-8888 ext. 1.

The race is scheduled for Sunday, June 13 on the 1.25-mile oval (photo, above) in Madison, Illinois, just across the Mississippi River from the Gateway Arch and St. Louis. It’s the third oval race of the season, after the race March 13 at Phoenix Raceway and the 111th Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge on Sunday, May 30 at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

HMD Sells INDY NXT by Firestone Team

HMD Motorsports, one of the most successful teams in recent INDY NXT by Firestone history, has been acquired by PV3 Enterprises, LLC and will compete as HMD | ENVE Motorsports beginning with the 2027 season.

The team will remain based at its Brownsburg, Indiana, headquarters under president Mike Maurini, continuing the organization built by Henry and Daiva Malukas since its founding in 2019.

The acquisition marks PV3's expansion into INDY NXT, the INDYCAR development series. PV3 entered American open-wheel racing through ENVE Motorsports, which made its USF2000 debut in 2025.

HMD has established itself as a championship contender in INDY NXT, earning two series championships since 2022. The team added another milestone in 2026 at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course, recording the first 1-2-3-4 finish in series history.

PV3 also has ties to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES through ENVE Composites, which sponsored Mick Schumacher's series debut in 2026 and supports reigning INDY NXT champion Nikita Johnson, who was announced Nov. 10 as one of Dale Coyne Racing’s drivers in 2027.

title: Who is Colton Herta? Everything to know about the American driver linked with a Cadillac F1 seat
excerpt:
Colton Herta is expected to be the next American driver to enter the pinnacle of single-seater motorsport through his ties to Cadillac, and this is everything you need to know about the former IndyCar star who is looking to break into Formula 1.

Colton Herta has been knocking on the door of F1 for multiple years now, with his first taste of the sport taking place at a private test for Alfa Romeo in 2021.

The American was already established as a multiple-time race winner in IndyCar at that point, despite being just 21 years old at the point of his first test.

Several years have passed since his first taste, and he is now looking to land a full-time seat through Cadillac’s entry into the sport this season.

Colton Herta is hoping to land a Cadillac F1 in the future

Due to the FIA’s strict superlicence system for new drivers who look to enter the travelling circus that is F1, Herta was unable to land himself a full-time seat at Cadillac for their debut campaign in 2026.

As those seats went to Sergio Perez and Valtteri Bottas instead, Cadillac’s top brass sought to enter Herta into Formula 2, in order for him to gain experience inside Formula 1’s ecosystem.

His role as a test driver has seen him take to the MAC-26 in several FP1 appearances over the course of the 2026 campaign, which is also an important factor in his development before stepping up to F1.

Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images

Following his most recent FP1 appearance for Cadillac at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Herta now has all of the superlicence points he needs for an F1 seat next year, but his performances in F2 have caused some concern.

The American has sorely struggled in his first term in the junior category with Hitech Grand Prix, and, after 10 rounds of racing, currently sits in P19 in the drivers’ championship with just 26 points to his name.

Still, Cadillac are hopeful that Herta is more comfortable in even faster machinery, and he remains a leading candidate for a seat at the F1 team for 2027.

Where was Colton Herta born? What is his nationality?

Colton Herta was born in Santa Clarita, California, and began karting at the age of six. By the time he was 10 years old, Herta started to race competitively and made his single-seater debut at the age of 13.

He races under an American licence and is the son of former IndyCar driver Bryan Herta, who runs his own team in the American single-seater racing category called Bryan Herta Autosport.

On top of that, Herta Sr. currently serves as the strategist for Andretti Autosport’s #27 entry, and used to serve as Colton’s strategist during his time in the category.

How old is Colton Herta, and when was he born?

Colton Herta was born on the 30th March 2000, making him 26 years old at the time of writing.

In 2019, just six days before his 19th birthday, Herta became the youngest ever winner of an IndyCar race in the category’s history.

Driving Harding Steinbrenner Racing’s #88 entry, he took the chequered flag at the Circuit of the Americas in first place ahead of Josef Newgarden and Ryan Hunter-Reay, respectively.

How tall is Colton Herta, and how much does he weigh?

According to Fox Sports, Colton Herta is 5ft 10in, making him around 177cm tall. His weight is listed at 141lbs, which translates to around 64kg.

Colton Herta’s IndyCar racing stats

Colton Herta made his IndyCar debut at the final round of the 2018 season, after just being beaten to the 2018 Indy Lights title by Pato O’Ward.

Nick Lachance/Toronto Star via Getty Images

His debut in the class also came two years after he raced in the 2016 British Formula 3 championship, where he subbed in for Lando Norris at Carlin Racing twice as the Briton pursued other opportunities.

Herta’s debut race saw him become the first driver born in the 2000s to enter an IndyCar race. Three months after he etched his name in the history books as IndyCar’s youngest-ever winner, he entered them again as he became the category’s youngest-ever pole-sitter, too.

Over the course of his 116 race entries, Herta claimed a total of nine wins, 16 pole positions and 20 podiums, before he set his sights on joining Formula 2 ahead of a potential seat at the Cadillac F1 team.

title: Inside Line Extra: Biggest 2027 Story at Chip Ganassi Racing?
excerpt:
Note: This series gathers the Inside Line panel to discuss the major storyline surrounding each NTT INDYCAR SERIES team entering the 2027 season. An installment on each team will appear at INDYCAR.com on Fridays.

Curt Cavin: Isn’t it all about Alex Palou (photo, top) given all the change within the organization’s engineering department? I actually think the changes make for a fascinating watch as we take evaluating Palou and his domination to another level. I mean, if he has another season anything like the past two, well, his legacy is at an all-time level. Seeing him earn a fifth consecutive series championship would be mindboggling given the talent throughout the field and even within his own team, keeping in mind that other teams have reorganized in a bid to dethrone him and the No. 10 car.

Eric Smith: While Alex Palou’s pursuit of a record-setting fifth consecutive championship is undoubtedly a major storyline, I’m particularly interested in watching Christian Lundgaard (photo, above, left). He joins Chip Ganassi Racing after recording back-to-back top-five finishes in the championship standings with Arrow McLaren, yet finishing third last season wasn’t enough to secure his seat. How will Lundgaard approach his first season with Ganassi? Will he put too much pressure on himself trying to prove McLaren wrong, or will he settle into his new environment and let his performance speak for itself? The opening stretch of the schedule presents an interesting challenge. Two of the first three races take place on street circuits, where concrete walls leave little room for error and can quickly punish a driver who overdrives. The other is at Phoenix Raceway, an oval where McLaren had seemingly questioned whether Lundgaard could deliver the results expected of him. With Ganassi carrying championship aspirations, Lundgaard's transition will be one of the team's biggest storylines to watch. How he handles the opening races, particularly on tracks that will test both his patience and adaptability, could set the tone for his entire 2027 campaign.

Arni Sribhen: There’s been a lot of change at Chip Ganassi Racing in the offseason. Foundational team members may have departed, but when you add new additions to what remains at the team, the sum of the parts is plenty strong to keep the 18-time INDYCAR SERIES champions at the top of the heap. How long that takes is the key question for 2026. Start with the engineering stand and who will work with Alex Palou, Christian Lundgaard and Kyffin Simpson (photo, above) in 2027. If the drivers work with familiar faces, this could be a long honeymoon phase for the new arrivals. But a slow start to these new relationships could be a season-killer before May, and we all know. Chip Ganassi likes winners.

Paul Kelly: During CGR’s two biggest peaks as a team, there were two elite drivers pushing each other to the limit. I’m talking about Jimmy Vasser and Alex Zanardi in the mid-1990s and Scott Dixon and Dario Franchitti in the late 2000s and early 2010s. That hasn’t happened in the last four seasons, as Alex Palou has laid waste to his teammates – and the rest of the NTT INDYCAR SERIES field. The closest any CGR teammate has come to Palou (photo, above) in the last four years was 78 points by Scott Dixon in 2023. Palou crushed Dixon by 259 and 300 points, respectively, in the last two seasons. Now that Dixon has left for Arrow McLaren, can team newcomer Christian Lundgaard return CGR to its days as a true two-headed monster that steamrolls the field? We will see, and the engineering and technical management changes at the team will make the unfolding of this storyline even more fascinating in 2027.

title: 15-Race INDY NXT by Firestone Schedule Announced for 2027
excerpt:
INDYCAR Development Series Builds on Historic Growth, Momentum

INDYCAR has announced a 15-race schedule for the 2027 INDY NXT by Firestone championship. The schedule features four doubleheaders and competition across 11 venues as the next generation of open-wheel racing stars continues its pursuit of driving in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES.

The 2027 championship will feature a diverse mix of street circuits, road courses and ovals, challenging a talented roster of drivers, engineers and team personnel at some of North America’s most iconic racing venues.

INDY NXT continues to experience unprecedented growth and exposure, reinforcing INDYCAR’s rising energy and momentum. The 2026 INDY NXT championship featured a record-tying 10 race winners, including a record-tying seven first-time victors. The season also featured the most passes on record in series history, with on-track passing records broken at nine tracks. Growth throughout the paddock resulted in an average of 24 starters per race in 2026 – the most in 17 years.

Television viewership on FOX Sports’ FS1 and FS2 increased 14 percent over the previous season. FOX Sports will provide a televised platform for every race in 2027, helping build on the series’ record-setting growth.

“As we have seen in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, INDY NXT by Firestone is in the midst of immense growth both on and off the track,” INDYCAR President J. Douglas Boles said. “With 10 different race winners last season, it is clear that the competition is as fierce as ever as drivers look to move up to the INDYCAR SERIES.

“With our partners at FOX Sports, the exposure and value of INDY NXT has clearly reached new heights. We know the 2027 schedule will provide another intense test for drivers and teams and produce a deserving champion to celebrate at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca.”

The 2027 INDY NXT Championship Road Map

The season opens Sunday, March 7, on the sunny Streets of St. Petersburg for the 17th time and sixth consecutive year. The series then returns to the Streets of Arlington on Sunday, March 21, for the second annual Java House Grand Prix of Arlington NTT INDYCAR SERIES weekend.

The first doubleheader of the season takes place Saturday and Sunday, April 3-4 at Barber Motorsports Park. Race 1 of the 2026 doubleheader featured a track-record 96 on-track passes, including 83 for position.

INDY NXT returns to the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course Saturday, May 15 as part of another historic May lineup at The Racing Capital of the World. The 14-turn, 2.439-mile layout produced a record 284 on-track passes in 2026.

June brings a busy stretch of competition at venues that all featured passing records and intense wheel-to-wheel battles in 2026. The series begins the month on Sunday, June 6 on the Streets of Detroit, followed by World Wide Technology Raceway on Sunday, June 13. The second doubleheader weekend of the season follows at Road America, with races Saturday and Sunday, June 26-27 on the iconic 4.014-mile circuit.

Following the series’ annual trip to Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin, the summer continues with a second consecutive doubleheader and a Fourth of July celebration Saturday and Sunday, July 3-4 at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course. The championship then heads west to Portland International Raceway on Saturday, July 31, before returning to the historic Milwaukee Mile for the final oval race of the 2027 season Saturday, Aug. 28.

The INDY NXT by Firestone champion will be crowned for the second consecutive year at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca following the fourth and final doubleheader of the season during Labor Day weekend, Saturday and Sunday, Sept. 4-5.

2027 INDY NXT by Firestone Testing Calendar

In addition to the race schedule, opportunities for driver and team development continue with a series of group and open tests in 2027.

The first of two preseason INDY NXT group tests took place Monday at Barber Motorsports Park, with an additional group test scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday, Jan. 27-28 at Sebring International Raceway.

Additional in-season group tests are scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday, April 28-29 at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course and Monday, Aug. 2 at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. The Laguna Seca test follows the series’ race at Portland International Raceway two days earlier.

INDY NXT oval open tests are scheduled for Thursday, April 22 at World Wide Technology Raceway and Thursday, June 17 at Milwaukee Mile, giving teams opportunities to fine-tune their cars ahead of wheel-to-wheel oval racing in 2027.

After this week’s announcement from Dale Coyne Racing that Nikita Johnson has joined the NTT INDYCAR SERIES team in 2027, the last four INDY NXT champions have full-time rides in North America’s premier open-wheel racing series next year. In 2026, 15 drivers with INDY NXT experience competed full time in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES, and 20 drivers with previous INDY NXT experience competed in the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge.

“INDY NXT by Firestone has been an ideal home for developing drivers and team personnel, and the diligent work from all of our stakeholders has produced meaningful results,” INDY NXT by Firestone Director Kirk Dooley said. “Once again, we have strategically added a testing schedule to an already impressive lineup of race weekends that will continue to provide an exemplary proving ground for INDYCAR’s next generation of stars. Combined with record paddock growth and exposure, 2027 is shaping up to be another exhilarating season.”

FOX Sports’ network assignments and tune-in times for the 2027 events will be announced at a later date. INDYCAR Radio will again provide audio coverage on SiriusXM channel 190 and the INDYCAR App powered by NTT DATA.

Outside the United States, INDYCAR LIVE will continue to provide live streaming coverage of all 15 INDY NXT races, along with all practice and qualifying sessions.

title: Colton Herta can say goodbye to a 2027 Formula 1 seat if Cadillac sale goes through
excerpt:
Colton Herta could lose his biggest backer for a 2027 F1 seat if the sale of Cadillac goes through, according to a report.

The American constructor’s owner, TWG Global, is exploring a sale of the team less than 12 months after its debut in Formula 1.

That is according to a report from Sportico, with ‘those familiar with the process’ putting the F1 team’s valuation at around $3 billion (£2.26bn).

Of course, a sale of the team would likely see massive changes happening behind the scenes, but a separate report from the Italian edition of Motorsport.com has also suggested that it would affect the future of F1 hopeful Colton Herta quite drastically.

TWG Global is Colton Herta’s biggest backer for a 2027 F1 seat at Cadillac

The reason why a sale could see Herta bid farewell to his dreams of racing in F1 is simple: TWG Global is the American driver’s biggest ally when it comes to his attempts to get on the grid, with General Motors keen on two other names instead.

Naturally, GM would like to continue with Valtteri Bottas in 2027 for consistency purposes. Cadillac’s efforts in F1 are still very much in their infancy, meaning any development work they may have already started with the Finn could be rendered useless if another driver takes his place.

The other name in the mix is Mercedes reserve driver Frederik Vesti. The Dane was in contention for a 2026 Cadillac seat before they settled on Bottas alongside Sergio Perez, and continues to be on the American manufacturer’s books through his entry with them in the IMSA SportsCar Championship.

According to the report from the Italian outlet, Cadillac’s top brass have been very impressed with Vesti’s performances in their endurance racing prototype, as well as the work he has been doing for Mercedes during their 2026 title-winning campaign.

Due to General Motors being the primary manufacturer and namesake behind Cadillac’s entry into F1, it means that Bottas’ and Vesti’s candidacy is unlikely to change, but the same can’t be said for Herta.

The American IndyCar race winner has fallen well short of the mark during his first season of Formula 2 this year, and has been losing favour inside the F1 paddock due to it.

Pundit Ralf Schumacher now believes Herta has ‘no place’ in F1 due to his woeful campaign, in which he currently sits in P19 in the drivers’ championship with just 26 points to his name.

On top of that, IndyCar commentator Will Buxton believes Herta would be in danger of becoming ‘the next Lance Stroll’ if he were handed an F1 seat next year.
